analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + RHM CEO Today / Prime Colour / Earnings Overview 9 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities closed Friday higher: SPX +31bps to 7376, NDX +135bps to 26989, RTY +89bps to 2754. NDX fell about 5% last week, a 4-week losing streak, and Semis are down about 28% over the last month.
The NFP print came in hotter than expected at 165k actual vs 75k consensus, and December hike odds rose to about 77%.
AI Semis (GSCBSMHX) gained +5.17% and Data Centers (GSTMTDAT) rose +4.99% on Friday. EU Semis bounced +1.6% while EU Defense sold off again, -2.4%.
11 of 20 European sectors have RSI above 70, the widest overbought reading since December 2023.
Goldman invites clients to a Rheinmetall CEO fireside today at 16.00 UKT.
Positioning: long $23bn S&P (71st percentile) and short $1bn NDX (35th percentile). There is big supply for S&P in a flat tape in both scenarios. The medium-term pivot level for SPX is 7547.

Basket idea: short the GS Diversified Staples Basket (GSXUSTAP). Earnings and dividend yield are unattractive relative to fixed income, growth is insufficient for the valuations, revisions are rolling over, and valuations sit in the 90th percentile relative to the last year.

Prime book: US equities were modestly net sold this week, with the largest single-stock net selling in 4 months partly offset by buying in Macro Products. Info Tech was the most net sold global and US sector, at a pace near the largest net selling weeks on record since 2016. Four of the top 5 net selling weeks in global Info Tech have come in the past five months.

Hedge fund performance: global momentum fell 4.6 SD and crowded shorts squeezed +3.7 SD. Systematic L/S managers lost 1.5% this week, a 4th straight down week, but are up 14.8% YTD. Fundamental L/S managers lost 0.4% and are up 8.7% YTD. Fundamental TMT managers lost almost 4% and are up only 1.3% YTD vs +25% mid-year.

European earnings are beating by 3.4% market-cap-weighted and 2.9% equal-weighted, slightly above historical norms. Misses are penalised more than beats are rewarded. Energy, Telecoms, Healthcare and Technology led the beats.
Prysmian has the highest exposure to Texas through its Encore Wire and Channell acquisitions, plus plans for 8 new medium voltage cable lines in the state.

Legrand has the largest datacenter business in GS coverage at 32% of sales and is more US-weighted than peers. It has derated significantly and has one of the most depressed non-datacenter businesses due to European residential exposure.
UniCredit beat net profit by 17%: revenues 7% ahead, costs 2% below, loan loss provisions 10% below. NII was 3% above, one of the strongest NII beats of the season, and fees were 3% above.

Hannover Re missed on solvency by 14pp, though the absolute level is fine, and bears may flag a small P&C reinsurance revenue miss. GS calls it the default long in the space. The stock was down about 1%.

Lancashire: Buy, PT GBP777, 15% upside, 12% dividend yield. GS sees underappreciated earnings resilience, a broader underwriting portfolio and less volatile earnings, so less contraction than in the previous soft cycle.
